propositions: Reconciler core functions pass transport/client parameters without type annotations, causing mypy to treat them as Any and silently permit calls to undeclared members, enabling defects like a357 where the Backend port omits methods the core unconditionally requires

Absolute imports like 'from rebar_reconciler._backend import TicketTransport' are silently widened to Any by mypy when ignore_missing_imports=true, because rebar_reconciler is not an importable package but a runtime sys.path shim, making annotations at those sites unenforceable regardless of their nominal type

Relative imports ('from ._backend import TicketTransport') inside reconciler modules allow mypy to resolve the Protocol correctly and enforce [attr-defined] errors on undeclared member access, as verified by reveal_type evidence

Four opt-in capability members (add_comment, set_relationship, get_issuelinks_map, get_comment_map) are carried as metaclass attributes rather than class body members, so hasattr returns True for the AST audit but mypy correctly omits them from protocol checking, making mypy strictly stronger than the existing audit at these sites

Capability member call sites must be narrowed to a composed Protocol (SupportsComments, SupportsLinks) via cast, never widened to Any or reverted to the shim import path, or the enforcement silently self-neutralizes while looking correct in review

The _TransportPortMeta metaclass is necessary for runtime conformance checking via uncached isinstance, making ABCMeta's subclass cache return False when a member is deleted, and must not be removed or replaced by splitting the class
